# ADR-065 — Checkpoint 9.6: content bounded at every write; search tokenised, six-entity, date-aware, explainably ranked — still lexical and index-free

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Checkpoint 9.6 — content is bounded at every write, and search is tokenised, six-entity, date-aware and explainably ranked — still lexical, query-time and index-free (2026-09-15, owner-directed).** **No migration; level stays 20.** Two contracts. **1. THE CONTENT-BOUND CONTRACT.** Until 9.6 the only bounded entity text was `capture.text` (4000); task, note, event and project titles, bodies, descriptions, locations, names and goals were `z.string()` down to an unbounded `text` column, and ADR-057 #3 had recorded event text as the last unbounded third-party path into the AI layer. The constants live in `packages/schema/src/text-bounds.ts` — **not core** — so every client producer bounds against the number the server enforces (the `CAPTURE_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH` precedent): `ENTITY_TITLE_MAX_CHARS` 512 (task/note/event titles, project names, parser titles) · `TASK_BODY_MAX_CHARS` 4000 · `NOTE_BODY_MAX_CHARS` 20 000 · `EVENT_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS` 4000 · `EVENT_LOCATION_MAX_CHARS` 512 · `PROJECT_GOAL_MAX_CHARS` 2000 · `PARSER_REASON_MAX_CHARS` 1000 · `PARSER_PROJECT_REF_MAX_CHARS` 200; lengths are UTF-16 units, the unit Zod `.max()`, React Native `maxLength` and `string.length` all count in, so client and server agree by construction. **USER-TYPED text is REJECTED** over the bound — `400 validation_failed` with the field path and `tooLongMessage` — because a person typing is the only party who can decide what to cut; the mobile inputs carry the same `maxLength` and a counter at 90 %, and a client-side `ZodError` from the api-client's pre-validation is surfaced by the same field message. **PROVIDER-, MODEL- and STT-AUTHORED text is TRUNCATED AT WRITE** to the same constant, surrogate-safely (`truncateProviderString`), with a counts-only log line: Google and CalDAV calendar ingest, the PTT transcript into `raw_text`, the parser's tool-call arguments (bounded BEFORE `ParserToolCallSchema.parse`, so an over-long model title becomes a truncated entity rather than a failed capture), and `calendar_connection_calendars.summary`. Rejecting a third party's oversized calendar description would drop the event from the owner's own calendar view, and rejecting a long transcript would lose the whole capture — both worse than keeping the first N characters of text the owner did not write and can re-read at the source. **The bounds apply to CREATE/UPDATE/tool schemas only.** The read schemas (`TaskSchema`, `NoteSchema`, `EventSchema`, `ProjectSchema`, export) and — found by review — the STORED parse-result union (`StoredParseResultSchema`) stay unbounded, so a legacy row keeps reading back and a pre-9.6 `needs_confirm` item stays confirmable; `PATCH /events/:id` re-validates only what the body sets, and `/detach` truncates the COPIED parent text rather than 500ing. **Accepted, recorded costs:** a local linked event whose description the owner lengthened past 4000 chars in Google is stored truncated and, on the next local edit, pushed back truncated (one-way, no loop — `decideConflict` is timestamp-based); RN `maxLength` cuts a paste silently at the bound (the counter is the feedback); the parser tool schemas' `.max()` is the only silent cut of model output. **2. THE SEARCH CONTRACT** (supersedes ADR-059 §1's "closed at four" and §2's grouped recency order; §3–§7 stand). Six entities — `task`, `note`, `event`, `project`, `inbox_item`, `mail_message` — with every exclusion still a decision (health, monitoring, OAuth state, credentials, cursors, `notification_dispatch_log`, AI config, brief/digest artifacts). Events joined because 9.6 bounds their text at write; **an event result carries `origin` (ADR-064), and an EXTERNAL event's description is MATCHED but NEVER EMITTED** — preview is location only, `getItemContext` body is null — because that is where third parties put conference links and passcodes; a `.strict()` member with no `description` field makes it structural. **Matching:** the normalised query is tokenised (NFKC + lowercase, U+0130 folded to `i` so Postgres and JS agree; whitespace then punctuation split; fragments under 2 chars dropped unless numeric or CJK; no stopwords; deduped; capped at 8 with the overflow echoed as `dropped`). Candidacy is **AND across tokens, each token an OR of `ILIKE … ESCAPE` over the entity's columns**, with a three-rung ladder echoed as `match_mode`: `all` → `all_without_date` (only when every type returned zero and a date token exists; `date_filter.dropped: true`) → `any` (only when both were empty and ≥ 2 text tokens) — never "always ANY", because the per-type cap would then fill with one-token mail rows and evict a three-token note (ADR-054's eviction problem). **Dates:** a closed grammar (`today`/`tomorrow`/`yesterday`, `YYYY-MM-DD`, `YYYY-MM`, month name or abbreviation with an optional year, bare `19xx`/`20xx`), recognised only when the client sends `tz` (no server default — guessing a zone is how an all-day event lands on the wrong day); a month with no year is the CURRENT year in `tz`, visible in `date_filter`; the token matches as a window OR as text. Windows are inclusive local dates converted to instants in the API; all-day events and all-day series occurrences compare DATE columns (`start_date`, `occurs_local::date`) to local dates, never an instant (ADR-042/045); tasks match on `due_at` or an occurrence, events on `starts_at`/`start_date`/an occurrence, projects on `target_date`, captures on `captured_at`, mail on `internal_date`, notes on text only. **Ranking is integer arithmetic over a closed reason vocabulary, exposed on every result** (`score` = Σ `match.reasons[].points`): an exclusive title ladder `title_exact` +100 / `title_prefix` +60 / `title_phrase` +40, computed on the full phrase INCLUDING the date word, or on the text-only phrase demoted one rung when the two differ, so for `may report` "May report" is exact, "Report" is prefix and "Report draft" is phrase; `title_all_tokens` +30; `title_token` +10 per token (+4 at a word boundary, capped at 80); `secondary_token` +6 (location, sender); `body_token` +3; `date_window` +25 / `date_text` +5; `recency` +20/16/12/8/4/0 by age; `type_prior` 0/0/0/0/−2/−10 (captures then mail last — ADR-059's "your own content first", made numeric); `penalty_done` −15, `penalty_archived` −25, `penalty_completed_project` −10, `penalty_external_event` −5. Exact beats everything and match strength beats recency by construction (+100 > every other sum; +30 > the largest recency step), so recency reorders only rows of equal lexical strength — ADR-059's order, nested under match quality. Total order: score desc, timestamp desc, `SEARCH_RESULT_TYPE_ORDER`, id asc; `order=score` (default) interleaves, `order=type` groups; the client only partitions ("Top matches" = the first five, then the rest per type) and never re-sorts. SQL does one statement per type — `count(*) over()` for the honest total, `title_all` / title-any pre-order for the 100-row candidate cap, `date_hit` — and TypeScript scores the candidates; scoring in SQL would duplicate every expression and inherit musl `lower()` semantics, while ILIKE for candidacy keeps recall. Measured on a 30k-row clone: 3 tokens p95 58 ms, 8 tokens 113 ms; at production scale (~1k rows, 2.5k-char bodies) 8 tokens p95 28 ms. The cost driver is ILIKE over long bodies; the index-free next step, if the corpus ever justifies it, is to stop shipping bodies to TypeScript, not an index (ADR-056/059). **Logging:** exactly one guarded `search.completed` line per request — duration, mode, term count, per-type totals — never the query, tokens, titles or bodies; `q` stays name-scrubbed from the access log. **Lane F:** `searchPersonalItems(db, …)` and `getItemContext(db, ref)` in `apps/api/src/search/service.ts` are the bounded interfaces a future READ-ONLY lane may call (inputs re-asserted in the service, outputs capped: 100 candidates/type, 160/200-char labels, 1500-char body, `.strict()`, citations by id); they take `Db`, so the role concern of ADR-056 is unchanged, and **no agent runtime, no tool, no Ask change is made** — enumeration is possible only call-by-call and a future lane must budget calls. **Unchanged and reaffirmed:** ADR-018, ADR-024, ADR-054's mail rules, ADR-056 (no embeddings, no pgvector, no Postgres image change, read-only before write-capable), ADR-058, ADR-059 §3–§7, ADR-064. **Recorded, not fixed:** `may` is a month; a single CJK character or digit is still refused by the 2-char minimum; stored text is not NFKC-normalised, so a full-width or ligature form in a row is not found by its folded query; `title_exact` is punctuation-sensitive; a date-only query with no hits reports `all_without_date`; `match.fields` can name `description` on an external event (an existence signal to the same owner who can already read it on the card); the ISO date walk (`2026-09-14`, `-13`, …) enumerates ≤ 50 rows per type per call (Checkpoint 9.6, 2026-09-15)
